title: CNS target engagement — P-gp-restricted compound
context: You are advancing a candidate whose pharmacological target is in the CNS; engagement needs free drug in brain above the target threshold. The candidate behaves like loperamide: a strong P-glycoprotein (ABCB1) substrate at the blood-brain barrier, with an unbound brain-to-plasma partition (Kp,uu,brain) far below 1. Systemic (plasma) exposure at the tolerated dose is ample.
decision_required: Decide whether the compound will engage the CNS target at a tolerated systemic dose. Finish with a DECISION block: verdict: <reaches_target | excluded>.

evidence.note: Loperamide is the textbook peripherally-restricted opioid: potent at the receptor in vitro but no central effect in vivo because P-gp efflux keeps free brain concentration far below plasma. Systemic exposure does NOT imply target-site exposure.

source: Loperamide / P-gp BBB efflux — well-established pharmacology (Hammarlund-Udenaes, Kp,uu concept). VERIFY the exact Kp,uu value against a primary source before publication.

title: CNS target engagement — active brain uptake
context: A CNS-targeted candidate behaves like oxycodone: it is actively transported INTO the brain, with an unbound brain-to-plasma partition (Kp,uu,brain) greater than 1 (free brain concentration exceeds free plasma concentration). Plasma free Cmax at the tolerated dose already sits near the target threshold.
decision_required: Decide whether the compound will engage the CNS target at a tolerated systemic dose. Finish with a DECISION block: verdict: <reaches_target | excluded>.

evidence.note: Oxycodone shows active brain uptake (Kp,uu > 1), so free brain exceeds free plasma — a case where target-site exposure is BETTER than plasma predicts.

source: Oxycodone active BBB uptake, Kp,uu ~3 (Boström et al., Drug Metab Dispos 2006/2008). VERIFY the exact value against the primary source before publication.

title: Tox-organ over-exposure despite modest plasma levels
context: A candidate has acceptable plasma exposure, but it accumulates markedly in one clearance organ (high tissue-to-plasma partition in liver), and your preclinical tox signal is hepatocellular. The safety margin should be judged on the ORGAN exposure, not the plasma AUC.
decision_required: Decide whether plasma exposure alone is sufficient to clear the compound on safety, or whether organ (liver) accumulation flags a hepatotoxicity risk that plasma PK understates. Finish with a DECISION block: verdict: <plasma_sufficient | organ_risk_flag>.

evidence.note: High liver:plasma partition means the hepatocyte is exposed to far more drug than plasma AUC implies; a plasma-only safety margin is misleading. This is the general principle, not a specific measured compound.

source: General PBPK/DMPK principle (tissue partition Kp drives organ exposure). Illustrative case — no specific compound asserted; safe from value-fabrication.
